bluf: Directive is a US B2B demand generation agency, 100+ marketing strategists by its homepage, ownership not disclosed, selling qualified pipeline through its Customer Generation methodology and mid market clients across ten industrial and technology verticals. The record shows it moving its search story onto AI: separate AEO and GEO service pages, 18 AI search articles, a Stratos AI platform and a DiscoverabilityOS model. A rival should know its client book on record is one slug, Zoom, which also buys from pmg and siege-media, that it sells B2B demand gen with no LinkedIn ads of its own, and that its sitemap shows 0 updates in 90 days.
doing:
The positioning line, a B2B marketing agency moving clients from MQLs to qualified pipeline via its Customer Generation methodology, organized into performance, commerce and communications divisions, decodes as a demand generation shop that sells pipeline rather than leads and packages search, paid media and content under one method. The headline claim, quoted as a claim, is 420+ brands served and more than $1B in revenue generated for clients.

One lead line scores 3, B2B & ABM: the title and H1 brand it a B2B agency focused on qualified pipeline, with ABM and demand gen pages. Four core lines score 2: AI Search / GEO (separate AEO and GEO service pages plus 18 AI search articles on GEO strategy and metrics), Content & Digital PR (a content division selling SEO led content for pipeline, 643 blog URLs with 208 updated in the past year), Paid Search (a paid media line for capturing high intent demand, PPC and shopping pages, its own Google ads) and SEO (the homepage leads on B2B discoverability and an SEO agency page). Paid Social, Programmatic & CTV, Data & Measurement and Email & CRM score 1; CRO, Local and Web & Product score 0. The service list adds Performance Creative, Revenue Operations, Marketplace, Shopping and Lifecycle Marketing. Proprietary: the Customer Generation methodology, Stratos and DiscoverabilityOS. No partners are listed.

AI posture in plain terms: it promotes Stratos, an AI platform for B2B client growth, sells AEO and GEO, and frames growth investment through DiscoverabilityOS; the move read marks P1 partial because no audited AI visibility product shows. Pricing signals: none. Recent moves: none dated; news and jobs are empty, and the one case study on record, Zoom, carries a lastmod of 2024-05-01. Conspicuously absent for a B2B agency: LinkedIn ads of its own, an office or founding year, any client beyond one, and measurement depth behind a pipeline promise.
clients:
The record describes a mid-market client type across technology, industrial and manufacturing, professional services, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, wholesale and distribution, telecommunications, construction and infrastructure, transportation and logistics, finance and insurance, and energy and utilities, with the US as home market and no offices listed. The book on record is one name: Zoom, evidenced by a case study slug titled Zoom - Directive, coded engagement named only (N0) because the slug describes no work. Observed needs are therefore 0 and the mix is empty.

Inferred from the sold mix, and said as such: a client of this agency most plausibly comes for B2B pipeline (N11), the only line scoring 3, with organic demand, paid performance and AI search as the channels the method runs through; the headline claim of 420+ brands served is the agency's framing and the record itemises none of them. Zoom is a client that shops: it also sits on the books of pmg and siege-media, the shared count being 1, and 1 of 1 clients on record is a name only, which the openings read flags as thin evidence of what the agency does for them.

What the base needs next, as a judgment tied to the edition: the Horus read places Directive best for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers), driven by AI Search / GEO and Paid Search, and most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) through paid search, SEO and content hours. Mid market B2B buyers are likely to ask for citation visibility and pipeline attribution next, which the record shows it selling as AEO and GEO pages but not as an audited product, and with Data & Measurement at score 1; moderate confidence, because no engagement is described.

openings:
The strongest opening is the LinkedIn contradiction: Directive sells B2B demand gen and paid social and runs no LinkedIn ads of its own. A B2B rival whose own LinkedIn account is visible can very likely lead with that in any pipeline pitch (moderate confidence: library records are point in time). Falsifier: Directive Consulting company page ads in the LinkedIn library at the next compile.

It sells AEO and GEO with no audited AI visibility product, so a rival leading with a citation number wins the AI search conversation (likely), and it runs paid search with no sign of ads tested inside AI assistants, so the first B2B agency to show assistant results sets the price. No public pricing model exists, so an outcome priced pipeline offer is a conversation it cannot have in public, against a firm whose whole pitch is pipeline. Its KJ6 exposure rests on paid search, SEO and content hours; the book is one shopping client, Zoom, plus 420+ claimed brands with no evidence, so a rival with described B2B cases has the proof it lacks. Monsoon reads Breeze with displacement 50.0, so price is a lever with part of the book only.
